headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Virginia's primary electric provider to establish rates that shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity to large energy users, such as data centers, rather than residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Senator L. Louise Lucas.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to High-Demand Users
news_summary: Virginia's legislature passed HB 1393, requiring data centers and other large energy users (25 MW or more) to pay for the increased generating capacity they demand. This legislation aims to prevent these costs from being passed on to other customers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires utilities providing water to data centers to regularly disclose the total volume of water withdrawn to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, communities.
news_headline: SB 553 Addresses Data Center Water Use Transparency in Virginia
news_summary: SB 553, passed by the Virginia legislature, mandates that utilities report data center water consumption to provide communities with clearer insight into local resource use. This aims to increase transparency regarding water usage, which has often been kept private.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring sound assessments near homes and schools and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
news_headline: Virginia HB 153 Mandates Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
news_summary: HB 153, passed by the Virginia legislature, creates a new permit process for high energy use data centers (100 MW or more). It requires sound assessments near residential areas and schools and allows localities to mandate assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
